newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Budapest BUX powers to new record on MOL, OTP Bank.
newsitem.headline: Budapest BUX powers to new record on MOL, OTP Bank.

text.p: Hungary's BUX share index opened at a record 7,168.36 forints on Friday on the back of a rally in chemical heavyweights and OTP Bank, traders said.
At 1007 GMT, the BUX index stood at 7,169.30 points, up 175 from Thursday's close.
"On Thursday afternoon Borsodchem, OTP and MOL rose significantly in London (on the SEAQ)," said Attila Berecz of Raiffeisen Securities.
"It was obvious that the rally would continue (in Budapest) and everybody wanted to buy".
MOL and chemicals TVK were the most actively traded. By 1008 GMT TVK rose to a new record high of 3,540 forints, up 40, MOL was up 135 to 4,325 and OTP Bank put on 435 to 5,650.

James Oates, director for central and eastern Europe at UBS in London, said Hungary's safe haven position in the region is behind the rise, meanwhile the amount of funds reaching the Budapest market was not that much.
"People still regard Hungary as a safe haven and I think probably this may be the case until after the Polish elections," Oates said.
"It's not so much enermous enthusiasm about Hungary rather it's more lack of enthusiasm for anywhere else."
Polish parliamentary elections are due on September 21.
However, Raiffeisen' Berecz expected the market to retreat somewhat by the end of the day.
"There never was such a high rise within one day," he said.
